## Modeling Action SR-12 in the WRCS SDM process

Action SR-12 proposed the purchase and/or lease of water rights on the Sacramento River to keep water instream in the lower watershed. The approach outlined here is adapted from functional flow theory and is a simplification for the purposes of the SDM process.

We use the flow-survival thresholds identified in Michel 2021 and create a synthetic hydrograph optimized for Winter Run Chinook Salmon (WRCS) life history and survival. We use the Action 5 CalSim III run as a baseline and splice the synthetic hydrograph in the dry years in the model. We also produce the total volume of water needed per month in each dry year in the time series to model the amount of water that would need to be purchased to achieve this flow regime.


**Pilot methods previously developed for Reorienting to Recovery (R2R)**

The R2R technical team met with a flow subgroup to determine the best way to model functional flows. The team started by looking at the Nature Conservancy's Natural Flows Database to understand dynamics in the Upper Sacramento system. Acknowledging that modifying flows will only affect parts of the decision support model (DSM) that use flow-based relationships, we decided to use flow-to-habitat and flow-to-survival relationships to determine when and how much flow we wanted in the Sacramento river. We compared this to the Natural Flows tool and the Calsim 2019 BiOp to provide some comparison of total flow volumes in these scenarios. This produced a wet and dry year monthly functional flow hydrograph, compiled into a 20-year synthetic time series based on the historical water year types represented in the R2R model time frame (1980-2000).

### What is a functional flow

California's functional flow include 5 distinct components of a natural flow regime for Chinook: fall pulse flows, wet season peak flows, wet season base flows, spring recession flows, and dry season baseflows.

![](images/Screenshot 2023-09-21 at 11.00.45 AM.png)

For more information on functional flow please refer to additional sources:

-   [Modeling Functional Flows in California's Rivers](https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fenvs.2022.787473/full#:~:text=Functional%20flow%20components%20in%20California,ecological%20processes%20in%20riverine%20ecosystems.)

-   [California Environmental Flows Framework](https://cfunctional flow.ucdavis.edu/sites/g/files/dgvnsk5566/files/media/documents/Cfunctional flow%20Technical%20Report%20Ver%201.0%20Mar_31_2021_DRAFT_FINAL%20for%20web.pdf)

-   [Natural Flows Database](https://rivers.codefornature.org/#/map)

### Tailoring functional flows to our system

Functional flows are hypothesized to be the best flows for salmon in our historical system. However, our system is highly managed so we needed to alter the salmonid functional flow to maximize benefit to salmon.

The R2R techncial team developed proposed functional flow monthly flows by combining characteristics of the [Natural Flows Database](https://cfunctional flow.ucdavis.edu/sites/g/files/dgvnsk5566/files/media/documents/Cfunctional flow%20Technical%20Report%20Ver%201.0%20Mar_31_2021_DRAFT_FINAL%20for%20web.pdf) with critical flow to survival migratory thresholds on the Sacramento River (from [Michel 2021](https://esajournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/ecs2.3498)). 

This original attempt did not maximize habitat so the technical team revised their approach to maximize modeled habitat and survival using the following principles: 

1) Optimize spawning habitat during winter run spawning time frame (May, June, July) based on the Upper-mid Sacramento flow-to-suitable-habitat curves documented [here](https://reorienting-to-recovery.github.io/DSMhabitat/reference/sacramento_habitat.html).
2) Fix dry season base flow at a low value to maximize water for Juveniles, use Natural Flows Database as a guide (August, September)
3) Optimize outmigration survival in last 3 model outmigration months (February, March, April). If water volume allows set migratory survival above 50%. If volume of water limited, set migratory survival above 20% (based on migratory survival flow survival thresholds on the Sacramento River (from [Michel 2021](https://esajournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/ecs2.3498)). 
4) Utilize additional flows for maximizing FP habitat in (October, November, December, January)

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Helper / Set Up Code
# Compare total flow volumne function 
compare_total_flow_volumne <- function(calsim_flows, natural_flow_flows, proposed_flow){
  all_flows <- bind_rows(calsim_flows |> mutate(type = "calsim"), 
                         natural_flow_flows |> mutate(type = "Natural flows Database flows"),
                         proposed_flow |> mutate(type = "Proposed Model functional flow")) |> 
    select(month, flow_cfs, type) |> 
    mutate(acre_ft_per_month = flow_cfs * 60.3707) |> #TODO confirm conversion 
    group_by(type) |> 
    summarise(annual_acre_feet = sum(acre_ft_per_month)) |> 
    rename(Scenario = type, "Annual Acre Ft Water" = annual_acre_feet) 
  
  return(knitr::kable(all_flows))
}

# Find Representative water year types
water_year_types <- waterYearType::water_year_indices |> 
  filter(location == "Sacramento Valley", WY %in% c(1922:2003)) |> 
  select(year = WY, index = Index, year_type = Yr_type) 


median_wet_year_index <- water_year_types |> 
  filter(year_type %in% c("Wet", "Above Normal")) |> 
  pull(index) |> median()

represenative_wet_years <- water_year_types |>
  mutate(distance_from_median = abs(index - median_wet_year_index)) |> 
  filter(distance_from_median < 1) 
  
# Representative Wet years are 1984 & 1996 - both .13 away 


median_dry_year_index <- water_year_types |> 
  filter(year_type %in% c("Critical", "Dry", "Below Normal")) |> 
  pull(index) |> median()

represenative_dry_years <- water_year_types |>
  mutate(distance_from_median = abs(index - median_dry_year_index)) |> 
  filter(distance_from_median < 1) 

# Representative Wet years are 1987 & 1994 - both .42 away

```

### Proposed Model Hydrograph {.tabset}

#### Dry Year Hydrograph

The table below shows monthly flow CFS for a dry year model functional flow on the Sacramento River. This table was constructed using the Natural Flows database and model survival thresholds.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
# Dry Years 
dry_year <- DSMflow::flows_cfs$biop_itp_2018_2019 |> 
  select(date, flow_cfs = `Upper-mid Sacramento River`) |> 
  filter(year(date) == 1987) |>
    mutate(water_year = as.Date(ifelse(month(date) %in% 10:12, 
                             date,
                             as.Date(paste0(year(date) + 1, "-", month(date), "-", day(date))))),
         month = factor(month.abb[month(date)], levels = month.abb[c(10, 11, 12, 1:9)])) 

sac_dry_natural_flows_database_hydrograph <- tibble(month = factor(month.abb[1:12], 
                                                        levels = month.abb[c(10, 11, 12, 1:9)]),
                                        flow_cfs = c(14100, 15700, 15600, 
                                                     9560, 4870, 2100, 
                                                     781, 626, 564, 
                                                     2230, 6060, 10100))

# Build Functional flow curve 
sac_functional_flows_for_model_dry <- tibble(month = factor(month.abb[1:12], 
                                                        levels = month.abb[c(10, 11, 12, 1:9)]),
                                             flow_cfs = c(
                                               8735, # Jan: Utilize leftover volume for fp rearing
                                               10700, # Feb: maximize survival per Cyril
                                               10700, # March: maximize survival per Cyril
                                               10700, # April: maximize survival per Cyril
                                               4750, # May: Maximize spawning habitat
                                               4750, # June: Maximize spawning habitat
                                               4750, # July: Maximize spawning habitat
                                               500, # August: dry season base flow
                                               500, # September: dry season base flow
                                               8735, # Oct: Utilize leftover volume for fp rearing
                                               8735, # Nov: Utilize leftover volume for fp rearing
                                               8735 # Dec: Utilize leftover volume for fp rearing
                                             ),
                            description = c("Utilize remaining water for FP habitat", 
                                            "Keep high for migratory survival (10700 for mig surv ~60%)",
                                            "Keep high for migratory survival (10700 for mig surv ~60%)",
                                            "Keep high for migratory survival (10700 for mig surv ~60%)",
                                            "Optimize for spawning habitat based on flow area WUA",
                                            "Optimize for spawning habitat based on flow area WUA",
                                            "Optimize for spawning habitat based on flow area WUA",
                                            "Set summer base flow to 500 cfs (natural flows tool)",
                                            "Set summer base flow to 500 cfs (natural flows tool)",
                                           "Utilize remaining water for FP habitat", 
                                           "Utilize remaining water for FP habitat", 
                                           "Utilize remaining water for FP habitat"))

knitr::kable(sac_functional_flows_for_model_dry)

```

The plot below shows the CalSIM modeled flows for the Sacramento River of an existing representative dry year: 1987. 1987 has the median water year index as provided by DWR out of all the "Critical", "Dry", and "Below Normal" years within our model time frame.


```{r, echo = FALSE}
combined_data_dry <- bind_rows((sac_functional_flows_for_model_dry |> 
                                  mutate(Type = "Model functional flow Dry Year")), 
                  (sac_dry_natural_flows_database_hydrograph |> 
                     mutate(Type = "Natural Flows functional flow")),
                  (dry_year |> 
                     mutate(Type = "CalSim")))
combined_data_dry |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = month, y = flow_cfs, color = Type, group = Type)) + 
  geom_line() +
  theme_minimal() + 
  scale_color_manual(values = c("black", "lightblue", "gray")) +
  labs(x = "Month", 
       y = "Flow CFS", 
       title = "Dry Year - Model Constructed Salmonid Monthly Flows")
```

The table below shows the annual total volume of water needed for each flow scenario. The dry year functional flow uses less water than the Natural Flows database functional flow and than the representative CalSIM year. 

```{r, echo = FALSE}
compare_total_flow_volumne(dry_year, 
                           sac_dry_natural_flows_database_hydrograph,
                           sac_functional_flows_for_model_dry)

```

### Creating a synthetic flow timeserries

In order to incorporate these functional flow into the model data inputs we combined wet years from the action 5 CalSim III run and synthetic dry year hydrograph to make a time series over the full 20 year period. We started by classifying years as "Dry" or "Wet" based on DWR water year type classifications. All "Dry", "Critical", or "Below Normal" years fall into the "Dry" category and all "Wet" or "Above Normal" years fall into the "Wet" category. 

The plot below shows this synthetic time series for the Sacramento River over the 20 year simulation period.

```{r, echo = FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Wet dry sequence 
new_year_types <- water_year_types |> 
  mutate(year_type = ifelse(year_type %in% c("Dry", "Critical", "Below Normal"), 
                                             "Dry", "Wet")) |>
  select(year, year_type) 

dry <- sac_functional_flows_for_model_dry |> 
  mutate(year_type = "Dry",
         month = match(month.abb, month)) 

# get action 5 wet year
# For calsim flow picked average wet year 
wet_year <- DSMflow::flows_cfs$action_5 |> 
  select(date, flow_cfs = `Upper-mid Sacramento River`) |> 
  filter(year(date) == 1996) |>
  mutate(water_year = as.Date(ifelse(month(date) %in% 10:12, 
                             date,
                             as.Date(paste0(year(date) + 1, "-", month(date), "-", day(date))))),
         month = factor(month.abb[month(date)], levels = month.abb[c(10, 11, 12, 1:9)]),
         year_type = "Wet",
         month = match(month.abb, month)) 

wet_years <- new_year_types |> 
  full_join(wet_year) 

dry_years <- new_year_types|> 
  full_join(dry) 

synthetic_hydrograph_sac <- bind_rows(wet_years, dry_years) |> 
  mutate(date = as_date(paste0(year, "-", month, "-", ifelse(month == 2 & leap_year(year), 29,      
                                                             lubridate::days_in_month(month))))) |> 
  # filter(year >= 1980, year <= 2000) |> 
  select(-year, -year_type, -month, -description, 
         "Upper Sacramento River functional flow" = flow_cfs, date) |>
  filter(!is.na(date)) 

up_sac_hydrograph_as_matrix <- synthetic_hydrograph_sac |> 
    mutate(upsacQcms = DSMflow::cfs_to_cms(`Upper Sacramento River functional flow`),
          year = year(date),
          month = month(date)) |>
    filter(year >= 1980, year <= 2000) |> 
    arrange(date, ascending = TRUE) |> 
    select(-date, -`Upper Sacramento River functional flow`) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = year,
                values_from = upsacQcms) |> 
    select(-month) |>
    as.matrix()
rownames(up_sac_hydrograph_as_matrix) <- month.abb[1:12]

usethis::use_data(synthetic_functional flow_sac, overwrite = TRUE)
synthetic_hydrograph_sac |> 
  filter(year(date) >= 1979, year(date) <= 2000) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = date, y = `Upper Sacramento River functional flow`)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue4") + 
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(y = "Flow CFS", 
       x = "", 
       title = "Synthetic Model Constructed Salmonid Flows for Sacramento River") 
```
